newsitem.title: USA: Viacom amid investors' picks - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Viacom amid investors' picks - Barron's.

text.p: Media giant Viacom Inc and news agency Dow Jones & Co Inc were among a series of stocks mentioned as worthwhile investments by major investors in a series of interviews in weekly financial tabloid Barron's.

Talking six months after a round-table discussion that was hosted by the tabloid, Mario Gabelli of Gabelli Asset Management said he liked companies that could become the target of a potential takeover.

"The ideal is to buy companies in front of takeovers," said Gabelli, one of nine interviewed in the tabloid's latest edition. "The owners-operators of small companies that dominate their niches are going to get high multiple bids from people who want to buy their companies."
He listed Sequa Corp, which provides parts and engine services to airline industry, as one of his favorites.
Gabelli also listed Liberty Media Corp, which owns Discovery Channel, and Viacom, which owns Blockbuster Video.
Michael Price at Mutual Shares said he sought companies that had built asset value, while their stocks remained stagnant. Price said he liked Dow Jones, as well as Sunbeam Corp.
Meanwhile, John Neff of Wellington Management said he liked Seagate Technology Inc despite the troubles the sector might have had recently, such as weaker demand for personal computers.
Neff said it had a "great balance sheet, hardly any debt, $2.2 billion of cash that they haven't let burn a hole in their pocket".
